rationale: Measured structure (current revision de4d95e2): the objective is the max-rank sum of device NCCL kernel durations over the step's exactly 13 fp32 SUM allreduces (calls d0938de87369efd500322679 x12 at 28,351,488 B and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b x1 at 157,541,376 B, cross_rank seq 21-33), RING SIMPLE over SHM/PCIe with 2 channels (nccl_tuning). collective_calibration measures near-wire completion at these exact sizes (1.98 ms per 28 MB, 10.60 ms for 150 MB, ~34.4 ms synthetic total), and in the execution_timeline captures the late rank pays essentially that floor (35.35-35.41 ms kernel sum) while the early rank pays 53.6-54.3 ms: its first ncclDevKernel_AllReduce spins 13.7-14.6 ms and the following kernels each spin ~0.5-1 ms. The cross_rank submit bounds locate the cause off the transport path: the early rank's CPU submits all 13 allreduces 12.5-12.9 ms before the late rank's, the offset is already established at seq 21 (before the first collective) and stays flat through seq 33 (grows only ~0.1 ms over the 29 ms submission window), i.e. the skew is accumulated before the final backward begins - during the 3 unsynchronized no_sync microbatches and the final forward, starting from the aligned before_run() gloo barrier - not during the collective window and not from wire time or algorithm choice. The clean paired evaluation shows the same structure at smaller magnitude (parent endpoints 38.09/41.31 ms, reference 39.70 ms, vs the ~35.4 ms late-rank level). The previous joint candidate (trial-2eafcccfdb, host-lean bitwise-identical GPT2Block path) passed quality and coverage but left the objective unchanged (40.12 vs 39.70, paired_gain_not_above_noise) and its previous-after capture still shows a 10.3-12.6 ms submit offset: symmetric host speedups do not reduce the relative inter-rank offset, so the remaining editable lever is to re-synchronize the ranks at the point where the offset matters. Communication-side edits are not legal or profitable here: the DDP wrapper (bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True), bucket inventory, no_sync schedule and the c10d::allreduce_ sites are frozen, the adapter must not alter the default reducer or the trace, and the payload is transport-bound so re-batching cannot go below ~34.4 ms. I therefore select the complete-workload project group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, target project.invoke) as an execution_plan boundary: it is the only observed callable that contains the accumulation loop and the final backward launch, and its direct replacement can reproduce the source step verbatim (identical zero_grad/no_sync forward+backward/loss bookkeeping/optimizer.step()/synchronize and the same discovery phase contexts) while inserting one barrier on the control gloo group that already exists in state (created in prepare(), already used by before_run()) between the final microbatch's forward and its backward - the last injection point before the 13 allreduce launches. The gloo barrier runs no NCCL kernels and installs no communication hooks, so the reducer, the 13 collective sites, their payloads and all gradients stay byte-identical. The two allreduce calls are included as affected calls because their kernel durations are the objective being targeted; they are not edit sites.
hypothesis: A gloo control-group barrier placed after the final microbatch's forward and immediately before its backward resets the accumulated inter-rank CPU submission offset at the last point before the 13 DDP allreduce launches; because the measured drift rate during the collective window is near zero (offset flat at 12.5-12.9 ms across seq 21-33 in the captures), the ranks then arrive at each allreduce nearly simultaneously, so the early rank's in-kernel spin collapses from the full pre-established offset (~3-6 ms in the clean paired regime, up to ~13-19 ms under discovery perturbation) down to residual drift over the final-forward/backward prefix plus per-bucket jitter. The max-rank communication_kernel_sum_ms is expected to fall from the current reference ~39.7 ms toward the late-rank near-wire level of ~35.5-36.5 ms (roughly 3-4 ms, 8-10%), with whichever rank happens to be early no longer determining the max. step_ms should be unchanged or marginally better: the late rank never waits at the barrier, the early rank's barrier wait (its previous lead) overlaps GPU execution of the final forward's queued kernels and merely replaces NCCL in-kernel spinning that was already on its wall clock, and measured step_ms (103-107 ms) has ample headroom under the 121.5 ms limit. Correctness is untouched: no numeric kernel is added, removed or reordered, so the exact cross-rank gradient replica check (atol=rtol=0), the serial-reference gradient/parameter checks, finite-loss and negative control pass unchanged, and the barrier executes unconditionally on every invocation (matching before_run's defensive pattern), so repeats, continuous steps and reset remain safe. Risks to be tested rather than assumed: if a share of the clean offset is GPU-side execution-rate asymmetry rather than CPU submission lag, the barrier recovers only the CPU share and the gain shrinks; if a fresh one-off scheduling stall lands on one rank after the barrier, that sample's max-rank sum stays high (the median of 3 mitigates); and the gain must exceed each pair's MAD-derived noise bound (last evaluation's bounds were 1.68/4.85 ms), which a ~3-4 ms effect should clear but is not guaranteed. Failure of this candidate would itself localize the residual excess to GPU-side or barrier-external causes, since the submit-offset mechanism it removes is directly observable in the collector evidence.
